To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a brute force feature search can generate representations for the Labeled Faces In the Wild face recognition problem that outperform previous state-of-the-art approaches, in spite that they require less training data and use a conceptually simpler classification backend.

a large scale feature generation and search approach can be used to generate feature sets that, when combined with standard machine learning techniques, outperform previous state-of-the-art results on the LFW unconstrained face recognition benchmark.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the best feature representation for the task at hand, given a large number of possible representations?
the following question: Given a set of raw pixel values, how do we best transform them into a representation that is most useful for the task at
the question of whether a large scale brute force approach to generating feature representations can outperform more traditional hand crafted features in a real world application.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a large-scale feature search methodology that has led to state of the art results in the LFW challenge set.

we have developed a new approach to feature representation generation that, in combination, with standard machine learning techniques, achieves state of the art face recognition results on LFW, outperforming the previous state of the-art approaches.
the proposed approach is a new, powerful and effective tool for the generation of feature representations in computer vision applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the feature representations we have generated are a new baseline to be used in conjunction with existing algorithms.

we have shown that the choice of feature set can have a dramatic impact on the performance of a given algorithm and that a simple, large scale, brute force search approach can be used to generate new, more powerful, representations.
a brute force, large scale search can generate representations which achieve state of the-art performance on the LFW unconstrained face recognition benchmark.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while feature engineering remains a critically important skill in modern computer vision, it is no longer necessary for the feature engineer to be human.
the search space of feature representations is large and complex, but can be systematically searched to find powerful representations that are well suited to the task at hand.
the feature representation is an important component of any computer vision system and can be improved by a large scale brute force search.
